holidays.name: Hobbit Day
holidays.description: A day for fans of Middle-earth to celebrate with second breakfast, elevenses, bare feet, and a hearty pipe-weed-free party. Fans around the world raise a toast to Bilbo and Frodo Baggins.
holidays.origin: Both Bilbo and Frodo Baggins share a birthday on September 22 in J.R.R. Tolkien's legendarium. The American Tolkien Society promoted the day, and it is celebrated during Tolkien Week, which includes the date.
holidays.funFact: Tolkien fans often mark the day with a feast of up to seven meals, since hobbits favor breakfast, second breakfast, elevenses, luncheon, afternoon tea, dinner, and supper.

holidays.name: National White Chocolate Day
holidays.description: A day to indulge in the creamy, sweet, and endlessly debated confection that is white chocolate. Chocolate purists argue about whether it counts, while fans happily eat it anyway.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food holiday that grew out of confectionery celebrations and social media. White chocolate itself was developed in the 1930s, when Nestlé began making it using surplus cocoa butter.
holidays.funFact: White chocolate contains no cocoa solids at all, only cocoa butter, sugar, and milk, which is why some chocolate lovers insist it is not technically chocolate.

holidays.name: Car-Free Day
holidays.description: A day when cities and citizens around the world are encouraged to leave their cars at home and walk, bike, skate, or take public transit instead. Some city streets get closed to traffic and turned into pop-up parties.
holidays.origin: It grew out of European car-free city movements in the late 1990s and became part of European Mobility Week, which ends on September 22. Cities around the world now take part in it.
holidays.funFact: Bogotá, Colombia, is famous for its weekly Ciclovía, which closes more than 70 miles of roads to cars every Sunday so people can bike and walk freely.

holidays.name: Elephant Appreciation Day
holidays.description: A trumpeting celebration of the world's largest land animals, with a focus on elephant conservation, protection from poaching, and honoring their intelligence and emotional depth.
holidays.origin: It was created by wildlife conservationists and animal lovers to raise awareness about the threats facing elephants, such as habitat loss and ivory poaching. It was inspired in part by World Elephant Day in August.
holidays.funFact: Elephants are among the few animals known to hold what appear to be funeral-like rituals, gently touching and covering the bones of deceased herd members.

holidays.name: Autumnal Equinox Celebrations
holidays.description: The first day of fall in the Northern Hemisphere is welcomed with harvest feasts, moon cakes, pumpkin everything, and ancient rituals. Day and night are nearly equal in length around this time.
holidays.origin: The September equinox has been celebrated since ancient times, including the Greek Eleusinian Mysteries, Mabon in modern Pagan traditions, and Japan's Higan, which honors ancestors.
holidays.funFact: Despite popular myth, you cannot reliably balance a raw egg on its end only on the equinox. It works on any day if you have enough patience.
